Title: Relationship between Debt-to-GDP ratio, Interest Rate, and IMF assistance on Sovereign Debt Sustainability

Hypothesis: Countries with a debt-to-GDP ratio exceeding 80%, combined with a high interest rate and a lack of IMF assistance, are more likely to face severe debt sustainability risks, resulting in a sovereign debt crisis. Conversely, countries receiving IMF assistance tend to reduce their debt-to-GDP ratio, lower interest rates, and enhance economic stability. Furthermore, IMF interventions are most effective in countries with a history of stable economic policies, low levels of corruption, and strong institutions.
